title: Seed-probe stochastic cache warmup and compatibility gate for FlashAttention v3 rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During staged onboarding of FlashAttention v3 (FA3) we observed intermittent latency regressions and increased p95 during cold starts and early decode windows. Root cause analysis shows a mix of: aggressive FA3 kernel activation for small batches, unprimed KV/prefix caches, and non-deterministic kernel prober behavior that oscillates under bursty traffic.

Proposal: Implement a seed-probe + stochastic cache-warmup subsystem and a compatibility gate that coordinates kernel selection with cache readiness signals. The subsystem will: 1) issue low-cost synthetic 'seed' prefill probes targeting representative shapes for a short time window after node start or model switch; 2) apply a probabilistic warmup policy that incrementally increases FA3 activation probability as KV/cache hit rates and latency telemetry indicate stability; 3) expose a compatibility gate at the kernel router that requires a short warmup SLO (hit-rate/latency thresholds) before full FA3 routing for production traffic.

Goals: reduce early-session p95 by >=20% for common short-dialog workloads, reduce FA3-induced oscillation events by 80% in canary, and keep steady-state tail latency change <= +3%. Keep additional cost (seed probes) under 1% of token cost per node.

Scope: runtime kernel-router, prefill orchestrator, prober harness, and canary rollout integration. Includes telemetry, dashboard, and canary/rollback playbook. Implementation will be parameterizable per deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
acceptance_criteria: Seed-probe subsystem implemented in runtime with parameters: probe-rate, probe-shapes, probe-duration, probe-budget-per-node
Compatibility gate implemented in kernel router: FA3 activation probability controlled by warmup state and telemetry thresholds
Telemetry: KV cache hit-rate, probe success/failure, per-kernel p50/p95 collected and visible in runtime console dashboard
Canary run (10% traffic) demonstrates p95 improvement >= 15% in cold-start window compared to baseline and no adverse steady-state regressions (> +3% p95)
Automated fallback: if probe budget exhausted or warmup fails, router falls back to FA2/compatible kernels and emits alert
Playbook and runbook documented with rollback steps and thresholds for SLA triggers
